expert_role: Facade engineer (independent reviewer, round 2, packet P12)

findings.issue: The spec says the City's TEUI/TEDI/GHGI limits 'were not read' and shows ENER results without a limit line. The open BC Publications consolidation of VBBL 2019 (Division B, Section 10.2, consolidated to 27 Feb 2025) is readable. Table 10.2.2.5.A1 gives TEUI/TEDI/GHGI of 120/30/3.0 for Group C over 6 storeys, 140/20/4.0 for hotel, 100/20/3.0 for office and 120/20/3.0 for Group D/E except office. Note (1) sends multi-occupancy buildings to Section 5 of the City Energy Modelling Guidelines. Article 10.2.1.3 also requires airtightness testing (10.2.2.21) and entrance vestibules (10.2.2.8) for 4+ storey residential and commercial buildings. A mixed-use tower is judged against occupancy-weighted limits, not one line.
findings.fix: Load the Table 10.2.2.5.A1 values as legacy_version reference lines (edition: VBBL 2019 consolidated 27 Feb 2025). Compute an area-weighted limit per occupancy mix, flagged as 'method per CoV Energy Modelling Guidelines s.5, unread'. Add airtightness-testing and vestibule flags to M06 and to the M01 entry sequence. Re-check against VBBL 2025 before any badge, and cite the open bcpublications URL as a new source record.

findings.issue: Glazing is described by 'glazing U/SHGC/VLT' with no assembly level and no facade system type. For a supertall curtain wall, whole-assembly U (frame, spacer and edge-of-glass) and the spandrel zone govern TEDI. The spandrel is opaque but carries curtain-wall framing and backpan bridging, so its effective U is far worse than a nominal wall. Splitting the facade only into 'glazing' and 'opaque' overstates performance. Fenestration labelling in VBBL 10.2.2.7(3) is per product (factory-assembled versus site-assembled).
findings.fix: Add a facade-system parameter (unitized curtain wall, window wall, punched window in a rainscreen wall, double skin) that sets default assemblies. Require whole-assembly U and SHGC (NFRC 100/200 or CSA A440.2 basis) rather than centre-of-glass values. Model spandrel as its own assembly class with its effective U. Name the BC Hydro Building Envelope Thermal Bridging Guide and the City Energy Modelling Guidelines as psi/chi sources to open; the BC Housing database page states no licence.

findings.issue: The dependency graph has cycles that a Grasshopper-like canvas, being a DAG, cannot evaluate. M06 depends on M07 (assembly build-ups) while M07 depends on M06 (areas by assembly). M02 takes glazing from M06 while M06 takes view scores from M02. M03 takes reflectance from M07 ('reflectance feedback') while M07 lists M03.
findings.fix: Split each loop into an upstream definition node and a downstream evaluation node. For example, an M06a facade layout node (WWR, system, openings) feeds M02, M03 and M07, and M06b (energy, bird and VLT checks) consumes M07 assemblies and M02 scores. Alternatively, mark the feedback edges as explicit 'iterate' links that the user triggers manually. State the evaluation order in the spec.

findings.issue: No module checks exterior solar reflection from a 244-305 m glazed tower onto streets, the below-grade link entrances, the public realm and neighbouring towers. Concave or faceted glass can focus sunlight, and reflected glare reaches drivers and pedestrians. This bears on human scale (40%) and urban integration (10%), and it is a standard facade-engineering study for supertalls. Only interior glare (DGPe) is covered.
findings.fix: Add an exterior solar-reflection metric to M06, run with three-mesh-bvh specular ray tracing at hourly sun positions. Report reflected-glare hours on the street-level and neighbour-facade receptors, and flag concave glass. No threshold until a source is opened, so status is team_assumption. Link the result to the glass reflectance and outer-coating choice.

findings.issue: Facade embodied carbon has no data path. The CLF BC guide excludes glass, yet M06 states that higher WWR raises 'glazing embodied carbon'. M07 inputs list concrete, rebar, steel and timber from STRC and only 'm2 per assembly' from M06, with no factors for IGUs, aluminium extrusions, spandrel backpans or curtain-wall units. For a fully glazed supertall, the envelope is a material part of the upfront carbon, and the WWR trade-off cannot be shown.
findings.fix: Add facade material categories (flat glass and IGU, aluminium extrusion with a recycled-content flag, steel and stone panels, unitized curtain-wall EPDs) taken from EC3/openEPD or CLF Material Baselines (CC BY 4.0), each with a data-quality flag. Compute kgCO2e per m2 of facade by system and WWR, and show the WWR-versus-carbon curve beside the TEDI result.

findings.issue: The method bins faces into N/E/S/W after rotating to true north. The downtown street grid is skewed roughly 45 degrees from true north (the spec itself notes the skewed north arrow), so a block-aligned tower's faces fall near bin boundaries. A few degrees of rotation then flips a face's bin and its WWR and solar rules.
findings.fix: Use continuous azimuth or 8 bins for M06 and M02 roll-ups. Show the results for +/- 5 degrees of proxy rotation, as M02 already does.

findings.issue: The WWR reference lines come only from the US ASHRAE 90.1 Appendix G baseline. Under the VBBL performance path, absolute TEUI/TEDI/GHGI limits apply and no 90.1 baseline is used. VBBL 10.2.2.3(d)-(e) (NECB path) does give a Vancouver-sourced reference: the reference-building WWR is capped at 40% and assembly SHGC at 0.36. There is also no line for the residential portion.
findings.fix: Add the VBBL NECB-path 40% WWR and 0.36 SHGC as legacy_version reference lines with clause numbers, keep the App G lines labelled 'US reference', and add a residential line or state that none exists.

findings.issue: The bird metrics describe UBC 'Tiers 1-3' with 55% as the floor. The Backgrounder has four tiers. Tier 4 sets no percentage but requires treating 'glazing near existing bird habitat or known migratory paths'. All tiers share fly-through elimination and the 5 m corner rule, and Tiers 1-2 require treating all glazing adjacent to vegetation and/or water. Above the 16 m zone and the sky gardens, the spec gives no treatment or risk rule for the upper tower on the Pacific Flyway.
findings.fix: Cite all four tiers. Add an upper-tower risk flag that combines night-lighting state, glass reflectivity and proximity to water (Burrard Inlet / False Creek, from the M02 proxy). Mark it as a judgement, not a tier result.

findings.issue: The treated-share formula '(treated glass + overhang area counted up to 1:1) / glass in zone' adds overhang area to glass area. UBC says only that overhang shading 'can also count as treated area up to a 1:1 ratio'. The usual reading is that glass within a height below the overhang equal to its projection counts as treated. As written, the formula can double count or exceed 100%.
findings.fix: Define the credit geometrically: glass area lying within a vertical distance of at most the overhang projection depth below the overhang counts as treated, without exceeding the glass area. Mark the definition 'per UBC citing CSA A460, standard text unopened'.

findings.issue: The EN 17037 glare metric says time conditions were not read. The REHVA table states the assessment as 'DGPe<5%', meaning the DGP level may be exceeded for no more than 5% of the reference period. Without that condition, an ingested DGP raster has no time criterion.
findings.fix: Encode the levels as 'DGP above 0.45/0.40/0.35 for at most 5% of occupied daylight hours (REHVA, secondary)', with view direction still unresolved.

findings.issue: The LEED v5 views metric omits rules stated on LEEDuser: views into interior atria may count for up to 30% of the required area, auditoriums, video-conference rooms and gymnasiums are excluded, and VLT must be 'above 40%' (the spec's good band says '40% or more'). The flag calling the LEEDuser page 'internally inconsistent on Option 5 points' no longer holds: Path 3 is 1 pt and Path 4 is 1-4 pts at 40/55/65/75%.
findings.fix: Add the atrium allowance and the exclusions, use a strict >40% VLT test in M02 and M06, list the 55% and 65% intermediate sDA steps in M03, and update the flag text.

findings.issue: Balconies and winter gardens are routed to 'other packets', but VBBL 2019 (consolidated 2025) Sentence 10.2.1.1(5) requires balconies, including enclosed ones, to be unconditioned space outside the envelope. This changes how an enclosed winter garden on residential or hotel floors counts for thermal performance, WWR and bird glazing.
findings.fix: Add a balcony/winter-garden facade type in M06, modelled outside the thermal envelope, and record the clause as legacy_version until it is checked in VBBL 2025.

findings.issue: Facade-engineering feasibility items are not routed anywhere: wind pressures at 300 m (which need a wind-tunnel study), seismic inter-storey drift for curtain-wall joints in a high-seismic city, perimeter fire containment and spandrel height, condensation risk at frames for humid residential floors, rainscreen and water management, and building maintenance units (BMU) and access for cleaning. The 'limits' text names some of them but assigns no owner.
findings.fix: Add a non-scored facade feasibility checklist to M06, with an owner packet (STRC, SYST) and status 'not assessed' for each item. Print it on the facade board notes so that entrants do not present unresolved glass corners or sloped glazing as buildable.

findings.issue: The status enum still lacks verified_secondary, proxy and legacy_version, so X01 must parse free-text status_detail and bracket tags in 'basis' to decide badges. Mixed details such as 'legacy_version (v4); verified_secondary (v5)' cannot be parsed reliably, and a parsing error would show or hide badges wrongly.
findings.fix: Add a structured evidence_status field (enum, one value per edition and source) in the platform data model now, even if the orchestrator schema lags, and have X01 read only that field.

findings.issue: The core release (M04 at 6-8 days, the M06 core cut at about 4 days and X01 at 2-3 days, so 12-15 person-days) must land by 13 Nov, 23 days away, alongside other packets. The M06 core cut also depends on M07 assemblies through the cycle above.
findings.fix: Define the M06 core cut with manual entry of whole-assembly U, SHGC and VLT (no M07 dependency), and defer the honeybee/gbXML export to v1.

verdict: Round 2 fixed every round 1 BLOCKER. Code jurisdiction, occupancy bases, evidence statuses (with the X01 gate), the embodied-carbon scope, FSR counting, the VGA model and the bird checks are now handled honestly. From a facade standpoint, the packet still treats glazing as centre-of-glass numbers with no system type or spandrel. It claims the City's TEUI/TEDI/GHGI limits are unreadable, although the open VBBL 2019 consolidation tabulates them. It also has dependency cycles a DAG canvas cannot run, and it ignores exterior solar reflection and facade embodied carbon. None of these blocks the 13 Nov core cut if M06 takes manual assembly inputs, so the packet passes with conditions.
